title: My Weirdly Good Bourbon Vanilla Tallow Balm Situation
body:
Okay so. I was sitting there. It was like, Tuesday night maybe? Late. The heater was doing that clicking thing it does. My hands felt like sandpaper. Like actual sandpaper. I’d washed them a million times that day and they were just done. Cracked by the knuckles. I remembered this jar I’d ordered on a whim a few weeks back. A tallow balm. Beef tallow skincare, specifically. The bourbon vanilla one. It sounded so strange I almost didn’t click buy. Beef fat? For my face? And hands? But the reviews were all people being weirdly intense about it, so I got it.

It arrived in a little box. I opened it tonight because my skin was screaming. The jar is small. Heavy glass. I unscrewed the lid.

Here’s the thing. The smell.

It didn’t hit me as “vanilla.” Not like a candle or ice cream. It was warmer. Deeper. Like if you baked something with vanilla and brown sugar a long time ago and the kitchen still remembers. Or like… the good kind of old bookstore smell, but sweet. Not perfume sweet. Just… cozy. The bourbon vanilla scent is the whole reason I even put it on. It makes the whole “rubbing beef fat on yourself” thing feel less clinical. More like a thing you do because it’s nice, not because you have to.

I scooped a little. The texture is weird. Not bad weird. It’s solid but soft, like cold butter. You rub it between your palms and it melts. It doesn’t feel greasy. It just… disappears. Into my sad, sandpaper hands. My skin drank it. I don’t know how else to say it. Five minutes later, I wasn’t shiny. I was just… not cracked anymore. The feeling was gone.

Anyway my coffee is getting cold. I’m gonna go heat it up.

## How I Ended Up Putting Beef Tallow on My Face

Look. I’ve tried everything. The expensive stuff in the fancy jars. The drugstore stuff. My bathroom cabinet is a graveyard of half-used bottles that promised “radiance” and delivered a rash. I have skin that can’t decide if it’s dry or sensitive or just angry at the world. Winter wrecks it. Spring, with its weird back-and-forth weather, is somehow worse.

I saw someone talk about tallow balm online. Grass-fed beef tallow balm. Whipped. From France, apparently. My first thought was, obviously, “you have got to be kidding me.” My second thought was… well, it’s just fat. Rendered beef suet. And the logic, when I read it, made a dumb kind of sense. They say it mimics human skin sebum. Like, our skin’s own oil. So it absorbs deep because it recognizes it. It’s not sitting on top like a silicone blanket. It’s going in and saying “hey, I’m here to help.”

I was skeptical. So skeptical. But my budget for magic creams was zero. This jar from this little Etsy shop wasn’t cheap, but it was less than one trip to the fancy makeup store. I figured if it was gross, I’d just use it on my elbows and be done. A weird experiment.

The bourbon vanilla scent made me click add to cart. I needed it to not smell like, you know, beef. Or nothing. I needed it to be an experience, or I’d never use it.

## What This Bourbon Vanilla Tallow Balm Actually Does

So my routine now. It’s not fancy. I wash my face at night. Sometimes I remember to use a cleanser. Usually it’s just water. Pat it dry. My face feels tight. That’s when I grab the jar.

Opening it is the first good part. That smell. It’s not a “scented tallow balm” in a fake way. It’s just… the smell of the thing. Warm. Comforting. It doesn’t smell like dessert, it smells like a feeling. A stress-reducing smell, for real. I take a tiny bit. Rub my fingers together. Press it into my skin. Cheeks, forehead, neck. Sometimes I do a weird little face massage because it slides so nicely.

It doesn’t burn. It doesn’t make me red. It just sinks in. My skin feels different in the morning. Not oily. Not dry. Just… calm. Even. I don’t know.

I use it on my hands constantly now. After dishes. Before bed. The cracked knuckles from that first night? Gone. I use it on my elbows, which were always rough. They’re… not rough anymore. It’s bizarre. This natural bourbon vanilla skincare thing became the only thing on my nightstand.

And here’s the weird part—I got one for my mom. She has that super dry, sensitive skin older ladies get. She called me last week. “What is in this stuff?” she said. “My legs don’t itch.” That’s it. That was her review. High praise.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

I’m not a before-and-after photo person. I don’t take selfies to track my pores. But I notice things.

My foundation doesn’t cling to dry patches anymore. Because there aren’t dry patches. I don’t get that tight, itchy feeling when the wind blows in spring. My hands look normal. Not like a mechanic’s hands. I caught myself just… touching my cheek the other day while I was reading. It was soft. Not “product” soft. Just skin soft.

I didn’t have a dramatic transformation. I didn’t turn into a dewy goddess. It’s subtler than that. It’s like my skin just finally shut up and decided to be okay. The background noise of dryness and irritation is gone. Now it’s just… skin. Doing its job. The bourbon vanilla tallow balm feels less like a treatment and more like a thing I do for maintenance. Like brushing my teeth. But pleasant.

I’m on my second jar now. I ordered it before the first one was even empty. That’s how you know.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, weirdly. The science-y reason is that it’s really similar to the oils our own skin makes. So it gets absorbed deep instead of sitting on top and clogging things. It’s like giving your skin back what it loses. For dry skin or skin that’s just pissed off from winter, it’s a game-changer. For me, anyway.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was terrified of this. My skin clogs if I look at it wrong. But this stuff? No. It’s the opposite. Because it’s so similar to our sebum, it actually helps balance things out. It doesn’t feel heavy or greasy once it sinks in. It just feels like skin. Good skin.

**What does bourbon vanilla tallow balm smell like?**
It’s hard to describe. It’s not like a vanilla candle. It’s warmer and a little deeper. Like vanilla extract mixed with the smell of a cozy blanket. Or the smell inside an old wooden cabinet that used to hold sugar. It’s comforting. It makes using the balm something you look forward to, not a chore.

So yeah. That’s my tallow balm story. I was a skeptic. Now I’m just a person with a jar of whipped beef fat on my dresser who gets weirdly excited about putting it on. If your skin is being difficult, especially with this spring weather, it might be worth a shot. I got mine from a small shop on Etsy. My skin’s happy. I’m happy. That’s all I wanted.
